I am a 49-year-old farmer in Quzhou County, and I have been working this land since I was young. My family has about 8 mu of flat, good-quality land on the North China Plain. Around here, the wheat-maize rotation is what we know best, and it is what puts food on the table reliably. Last October, I sowed winter wheat with an improved variety like Jimai 22 — it handles our winters well and gives steady yields. Now that spring has arrived, I am already managing that wheat crop. I will irrigate it four times in total, including the winter irrigation I already gave it, plus water at jointing, heading, and grain filling. For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer as a base and topdress with urea; all told, I use about 58 kg of nitrogen, 25 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I did rotary tillage before sowing last autumn, and now I spray for insects twice, apply herbicide once, and add one fungicide spray to keep rust and powdery mildew away. I expect about 1,050 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize — something like Nongda 372 or Denghai 605 — using no-tillage direct seeding right into the wheat stubble. That saves time, fuel, and labor during the busy summer season. Maize does not need as much water here; two irrigations are usually enough, one at sowing if it is dry and another at the big trumpet stage. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress with urea later, using about 50 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. For crop protection, I spray insecticide twice and herbicide once; maize around here does not usually need fungicide. I expect roughly 1,100 kg per mu from the maize. I stopped growing cotton years ago — the price bounces around too much and the labor is exhausting. Wheat and maize have stable minimum purchase prices from the government, so I know I will at least break even. I keep a tiny vegetable plot by the house for family eating, but my real focus and income come from these two grain crops.
